title: tri-sdk credential shim, stream ergonomics, and version alignment
author: Diego Ramos
release_notes: Tri-SDK: introduce lightweight credential shim and CompactStreamFacade; unify retry presets and minor behavioral parity across Python/TypeScript/Go; bump package versions (py 1.16.0, ts 2.4.0, go v1.9.3). No public API breaking changes expected for majority of users; small edge-case change to stream close ordering documented.
description: Motivation: customers reported inconsistent stream warmup behavior and duplicated credential prefetch across SDKs causing extra auth calls and memory churn. This PR introduces a small, language-idiomatic credential shim and a compact streaming facade to harmonize ergonomics across Python, TypeScript, and Go. Goals: 1) eliminate redundant credential prefetch on stream creation, 2) expose an explicit close()/aclose()/Close() on streaming handles to make shutdown deterministic, 3) align retry/backoff presets used by streaming reconnection paths across SDKs, and 4) bump SDK versions to publish the coordinated surface changes. What changed: added a lightweight credential_shim that centralizes token rotation and offers an async prefetch hook; introduced CompactStreamFacade in TS and a matching StreamHandle decorator in Go/Python that provides deterministic close semantics and a small ReadableStream-like wrapper for push/pull patterns; normalized retry profiles used by stream reconnect paths and added a new "warmup" preset for low-latency interactive workloads; updated examples and docs and bumped package versions. Testing: unit tests added for token prefetch de-dup, stream close ordering, and retry-weighted reconnection; integration tests run against local canary serving to validate rollback and tandem token rotations. Migration notes: consumers who relied on implicit GC-driven stream teardown should call the explicit close APIs to guarantee handler shutdown; we provide a deprecation shim that logs a one-time warning for one release. Checklist: [x] design review and perf postmortem, [x] unit tests, [x] integration tests, [x] docs update, [x] version bumps. Related: ENG-1293, SUP-4821.
